title: The roofline
goal:
Implement the model from Section 3 of the paper. Attainable performance is the smaller of the compute roof and the bandwidth roof. Units are GFLOP/s for `peak`, GB/s for `bw`, and FLOPs per byte for `intensity`.

- `attainable(intensity, peak, bw)` returns $\min(\text{peak}, \text{bw} \times \text{intensity})$. It must accept a NumPy array of intensities and return an array of the same shape.
- `ridge_point(peak, bw)` returns the intensity where the two roofs meet.
- `is_memory_bound(intensity, peak, bw)` returns `True` when the kernel sits on the slanted part of the roof. A kernel exactly at the ridge point is not memory-bound.

The tests use the Opteron X2 from the page: peak 17.6 GFLOP/s and 15 GB/s.
hints: `np.minimum(a, b)` takes the element-wise minimum and broadcasts a scalar against an array. Python's `min` doesn't work on arrays.
The ridge point is where `bw * intensity == peak`. Solve for `intensity`.
Compare the bandwidth roof with the peak: the kernel is memory-bound when `bw * intensity < peak`.
